title: Lower the within-cell halo exponents to 11, 24, 26, 26 and 6 (no new κ)
body:
## Question

#4451 shows that a downward weight with absolute error below `4η` has relative error below `δ = 2^{2-32760p}`, which is stronger than `1/(16p^2)`. Do the within-cell exponents 12, 26, 28, 28 and 6 still apply, and is `16p^2-1` still the inverse ceiling?

## Result

Under the ideal-gap hypothesis, both rounded off-sums stay strictly below `(1-1/(8p^2))/(1-δ)`. The Neumann bounds are strictly less than

```text
U = 8 p^2 (D-4) / (D - 32 p^2),    D = 2^{32760 p}.
```

Then `8p^2 < U < p^6` and `U < 16p^2-1`. At `p=2`, `U > 32 = p^5`, so `U^2 > p^{10}`. Also `U^2 < p^{11}`. The same polynomial argument as #4439, with spectral endpoint 11, gives error below `p^6 exp(-p^2)`, bandwidth below `p^{26}`, and the same agreement distance.

| Role | Under `1/(16p^2)` | Under `δ` | Smallest |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Spectral endpoint | 12 | 11 | 10 fails at `p=2` |
| Series length | 26 | 24 | 23 fails at `p=2` |
| Bandwidth | 28 | 26 | 25 fails |
| Agreement distance | 28 | 26 | 25 fails |
| Normalizer | 6 | 6 | 5 fails at `p=2` |

So 12, 26, 28, 28 and 6 still apply. The first four are no longer smallest. The normalizer stays 6. The older ceiling `16p^2-1` remains a legal upper bound and is strictly coarser than `U`.

**Claim type:** conditional exponent arithmetic inside one cell. **No new κ.** The ideal gaps `1/(8p^2)` stay hypotheses. The #4100 notes keep 20, 42, 45, 48 and 100. Across-cell transfer is the open question, now that #4449 supplies `0 ≤ H ≤ n`.

## Test plan

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/gaussian-delta-exponents
```
